A future study, with a bigger sample and more research tools, when Covid-19 pandemic ends, might contribute to a better understanding of digital transformation process in Greece under circumstances different than those of a pandemic crisis.

articleTitle: Real-time Age-Group and Accurate Age Prediction with Bagging and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Age prediction based on facial images has become a vital part in many scenarios since the human face contains most important bio-metric characteristics from race, gender to age. As a result, automatic age prediction has gained its potential importance. This paper addresses two approaches to this problem: accurate age and age-group prediction, both using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and deep neural networks (DNNs) - two fundamental deep learning techniques, in combination with computer vision library, OpenCV to aid in classifying input images. This work is distinguished by two main key contributions. The first is feature extraction, where convolutional activation features could be obtained through using a novel hierarchical aggregation based neural networks to learn aging features from an abundant number of training data. The second contribution is the features classification part, in which we apply the Softmax Regression (SR) classifier to perform accurate age prediction whereas age-group prediction uses majority vote classifier. The results showed that the number and the quality of training images and subjects in the training dataset play a significant role in improving the accuracy of this work. The experimental results showed satisfactory and promising performance, which indicates another direction of further development and optimization of deep learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Process reengineering and optimization for innovation performance: An application to detergent manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Today's manufacturing industries are working in dynamic market climates. They are facing rapid technological evolution, as well as demand, supply, and lead-time uncertainty fluctuations. The detergent industry is one of the most important and active factories that are meeting the challenge of increasing global production capacity. These future generation companies are expected to reengineer their processes in such a dynamic context by applying continuous improvement policies in order to minimize costs, raise quality and perform effectively. To reach such a purpose, a methodology, based on structured process reengineering procedures, is proposed for a leading international company specialized in household detergents, disinfectants, and laundry cleaning products. Relying on complementarities and synergies between the adopted models, we begin by defining and analyzing the actual processes of the company to detect wastes and bottlenecks. After streaming the current processes, solutions based on process automation are proposed and a future state map is designed to eliminate the wastes measured. The actual and future process maps are analyzed to assess the overall improvement realized by redesigning and automating processes. The findings also highlight the effective interactions between the two popular frameworks: Business Process Modeling and Lean Management, using notably the BPMN and VSM techniques.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Methods applied to Intrusion Detection: Survey, Taxonomy and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Because of the popularity of the Internet of Things (IoT), the rapid expansion of computer networks, and the vast number of important applications, cyber security has lately garnered a lot of attention in today's security issues. As a result, identifying different cyber-attacks or abnormalities in a network, as well as constructing an efficient intrusion detection system that plays a key part in today's security, is becoming increasingly critical. Such a data-driven intelligent intrusion detection system may be built using artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning techniques. This survey provides a thorough review of Machine Learning (ML) techniques for cybersecurity intrusion detection systems, with an emphasis on new Deep Learning-based approaches (DL). The study examines current techniques in terms of intrusion detection processes, performance outcomes, and limits, as well as whether or not they use benchmark datasets to provide a fair assessment. In addition, a thorough examination of cybersecurity benchmark datasets is provided. This article aims to offer a roadmap for readers interested in learning more about the potential of deep learning techniques for cybersecurity and intrusion detection systems, as well as a thorough examination of the benchmark datasets used to train DL models in the literature.

articleTitle: Towards the RES Development: Multi-Criteria Assessment of Energy Storage Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: This paper presents the MCDM approach for recommending the most advantageous energy storage variant among the many available alternatives. Interest in energy storage is growing rapidly with the increasing popularity of photovoltaic systems. The motivation is that the further development of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) requires an efficient way of storing the produced energy. Energy storage allows accumulating the excess energy generated by a PV system and later recovering it without losses. Due to the many different technical parameters of energy storage devices, the MCDM approach is preferable because it enables reliable evaluation considering many criteria, even in the lack of expert knowledge about these devices. The authors included COMET, MOORA, TOPSIS, and PROMETHEE II in the proposed MCDM approach. A comparative analysis of the final rankings was then performed using two ranking correlation coefficients. The high convergence of the obtained results confirms the reliability and usefulness of the selected MCDM methods for recommending energy storage considering chosen criteria in e-commerce systems.

articleTitle: Impact of Work-Life Balance on Job Performance - Analysis of the Mediating Role of Mental Well-Being and Work Engagement on Women Employees in IT Sector
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The current research aims to examine the impact of work-life balance on work engagement, mental well-being and job performance among working women in the IT sector. We also tried to evaluate the mediate effect of mental well-being and work engagement on the direct relationship of work-life balance and job performance. The data is collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed using SMART PLS and Process Hayes to develop the model and to check mediation, respectively. 128 working women employees are interviewed through a structured interview using convenience sampling. All the respondents are women employees working in IT companies located in Mumbai, India. Current research suggests all the companies manage the work-life balance of working women in IT companies. In the current study, the researcher found an insignificant relationship between work-life balance and job performance. The insignificant relationship is found between work engagement, and job performance is found. A significant positive relationship is found between work-life balance and mental well-being, job performance and mental well-being, work-life balance, and work engagement. The mental well-being and work engagement is not found as a mediator in the direct relationship of work-life balance and job performance. In India, women are responsible for all the household activities; hence it is essential to manage the work-life balance of those working women. The current research is helpful to all the HR managers to frame policies that will help to maintain work-life balance and ensure high performance and low turnover intention among women employees.

articleTitle: Systemic Decision Business Opportunities Model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a universal systemic decision model for managerial decisions applying to business opportunities in quantum computing as an illustrative example. A systemic business decision model is formulated which orients on long term trajectorial high impact global human decisions. We give as a background an overview of business opportunities models and the state of the art of Quantum Computing (QC) as an emerging technology trend and extract from this a perspective towards future applications. Finally, we focus on Academic Spin-off Quantum Computing Business Opportunities: (1) How do they apply to QC from a systemic standpoint? (2) How can business opportunities be derived from this from the actual technology situation? (3) What does this mean for the ecology of start-ups, the industry and society as a whole, represented by all scales of societal decisions, as a snapshot? (4) How can this, as a whole, be coordinated and ordered with a systemic business intelligence tool?

articleTitle: Indicators of injury severity of truck crashes using random parameter logit modeling
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Crashes involving trucks were more severe and often results in fatal injury crashes. There is an innumerable number of explanatory factors that play an essential role for the accidents involving freight vehicles to happen like roadway design, weather conditions, and driver perception. The Torkham border highway acts as a lifeline for trade between Pakistan and Afghanistan; therefore, its safety analysis is essential. The objective of this study was to perform an extensive study to identify the risk factors that contribute to the injury severity of freight vehicle crashes using explanatory variables. A total of 2500 observations of road traffic crashes were obtained from May 2001 to August 2021 from the accidents recording agencies. Methodologically, a random parameter logit model with heterogeneity in mean and variances was employed to estimate the risk factor using three severity categories namely minor, major, and fatal injuries. 17 explanatory variables show a significant institution with the injury severity of freight vehicles on the Torkham road. Among the identified factors, it was revealed that the probability of the fatal injury severity increases with the increased exposure to freight vehicles; driver-related factors, temporal and environmental characteristics, they were found significant. The significance of this study is to account for the heterogeneity in mean and variances to observe the factors in real-time. Based on the findings, the authors recommend road safety strategies for the mitigation of truck crashes that could proliferate the safe environment for the truck drivers.

articleTitle: Decision Analysis on the Financial Management of Shipping Companies using Goal Programming Model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Being capital intensive, the shipping industry's asset and liability management (ALM) is very distinctive due to its difficulty for speculation. Credits and financing of the shipping industry are constrained especially in developing countries. With this, this paper aims to analyze the ALM of shipping companies in Malaysia with goal programming (GP) model to determine the balanced blend of assets, liabilities and equities for their profits, earnings and optimum management item. Malaysian shipping companies face many disturbances since the great lockdown and are now moving into the recovery phase. Hence a study on the ALM of the shipping companies would provide an overview of the assets and liabilities to make decisions on investment, expansion and succession activities. This GP model is enhanced by taking the best values of all goals as the target values to ensure better comparison of goal achievements. The results show that COMPLET, FREIGHT and HARBOUR have achieved the asset, equity and optimum management item goals. COMPLET and HABOUR have also achieved the profit and earnings goals. The quantifiable optimal allocation of resources serves as improvement values to revamp the companies. The overachievements and underachievement of goals provide insights for the shipping companies in their investment decisions, financing and risk management strategies. Even though GP model is highly flexible, the shipping industry must satisfy the interests of all the stakeholders simultaneously which cannot be fully reflected in this model. Future studies may include expert opinions which can then integrate with other multi-criteria decision-making model to reduce subjectivity.

articleTitle: Industry 4.0 in maintenance: Using condition monitoring in electric machines
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Industry traditionally considered maintenance as a cost and a necessity to replace equipment and machines, but the path has changed to better focus on maintenance to prevent faults and it was designated as predictive. The ones motivated to take these advantages are faced with two of the biggest barriers: the investment it requires and the difficulty to develop algorithms. The costs of installation are still high, but the avoided costs surpass it. Also, Internet of Things (IoT) has brought a big shift, which is been known as the industry 4.0. One of the potentials in maintenance is the conditioning monitoring. Condition monitoring sensors and devices are now linked to maintenance platforms, providing real-time data. This new connectivity is both more affordable and easier to implement than predictive maintenance. Real-time data allows managers to adjust preventive maintenance plans while providing greater reliability. At the same time, artificial intelligence manages this data to recognize patterns, which is one of the most promising advances in digital reliability. So, regardless of the ability to immediately implement a preventive maintenance plan, condition monitoring is an asset itself. The present paper presents the common faults on electric machines, their effects, their impact on the industry and the main techniques on condition control to prevent them. It is also added the reflection on the use of IoT to enhance the potential of condition control maintenance. The implementation of continuous improvement actions throughout the life of the equipment allows to increase efficiency, either by overcoming weaknesses or by adapting production or operational capacities to processes, production or maintenance, avoiding under maintenance or over maintenance and minimizing operating costs.

articleTitle: The Impact of Management by Objectives on Employee Behaviour and Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The present research is aimed at exploring the impact of management by objectives (MBO) on employee behaviour and performance. To fulfil the objective of the present research, a review of the available literature was conducted. Management by Objectives is one of the most recent performance appraisal techniques managers apply to assess the performance of their employees. The goal setting process can be carried out by managers in collaboration with employees. This contributes to the motivation of the employees and to the effect. In addition, feedback is an important part of the MBO process. Above all, goals have a positive and significant influence on the behavior and performance of employees. A systematic literature search is used. The researcher approaches MBO as an independent variable; Employee behavior and performance as dependent variables; and the relationship between them all, as shown in previous research. Also the correlation among the variables is based on a meta-analysis. Findings show that MBO process creates a state of employee motivation, satisfaction, commitment, loyalty which show the behaviour of the employees. This in turn leads to improving the performance of the employees. Also, the goal set must be realistic, acceptable and relate to the functions of the organization. Furthermore, feedback is an important part of the MBO process which plays great roles in making the employees feel they are valued and what they do is appreciated. This also contributes to enhancing employees' performance. When employees receive feedback on their performance, their behavior improves.

articleTitle: Financial decision making and Foreign Direct Investment in the era of COVID-19 and beyond: Evidence from India
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) plays an imperative role for the growth of the business sector and contributes to a significant level towards economic growth. It facilitates flow of funds towards poor and developing countries to establish business units, to raise their production capacity and to offer ample employment opportunities to unemployed youth, to raise labor skills by transfer of technology and managerial know-how, thereby FDI tries to assimilate domestic economy with the global economy. But because of COVID-19, there is a massive setback for various countries in attracting FDI, India is not an exception to it. The present study tries to critically analyze the impact of ongoing pandemic on FDI inflows in India. Thus, an attempt has been made in this study to ascertain the impact of COVID-19 on FDI in India and make recommendations to attract more FDI.

articleTitle: Customer Satisfaction Analysis to Improve the Library Services Using Fuzzy Servqual Method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Amidst the ascension of more advanced technology in the digital era, information could easily be obtained at the fingertips. Despite risking being obsolete, libraries have remained essential as primary sources of information, research, and educational tools, especially for students and educators alike. As one of the public institutions, libraries strive to provide high-quality and optimal service to their customers. This research is conducted to amount the customer satisfaction and the service quality of the library users and determine if the quality of service is as perceived. An observation period was performed at which 100 data were collected and calculated using Fuzzy Service Quality (Servqual) at East Kalimantan Regional Library. The conclusion could be drawn that customer satisfaction was indeed low. Overall, this was suggested by the vast GAP value for the Tangibles dimension, which read −10.67. Customers were also left disappointed in particular by the quality of free Wi-Fi service, which read −14.92. This means that improvements are needed in those aforementioned areas.

articleTitle: Effect of Information on Online Purchase Intention: An Extension of Information Acceptance Model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Online information research has been a popular pastime among consumers in recent years. The idea of word of mouth has regained popularity, just as social media, websites, blogs, and other online platforms have grown in popularity. It has been shown that information task-fit reduces specific but frequent information deficiencies for visitors. This study investigates purchase intentions by combining predictions from information features and consumers' information-related behaviours, and it proposes an information acceptance model in which an information task-fit is created to contribute to buying intention. This study surveyed 205 customers who used social media or web sites to find products through quantitative research. The result pointed out that the information characteristics as quality, credibility, and task-fit positively impact information usefulness, affecting purchase intention and information adoption. Besides, information adoption has a positive antecedent of purchase intention.

articleTitle: Efficacy of Deep Learning Approach for Automated Melanoma Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Melanoma is considered the most perilous type of skin cancer. However, differentiating lesions of melanoma from non-melanoma lesions has proven difficult. For this purpose, many Computer-Assisted Automatic Diagnosis Technologies are proposed in the past. Due to the complicated visual properties of images of skin lesions, which include inhomogeneous fuzzy boundaries and features, they have been limited in their performance. The use of computer-aided systems to diagnose skin lesions is becoming more common. Researchers have recently expressed a growing interest in developing computer-assisted diagnosis methods. In this research, a deep learning system for automated melanoma segmentation and lesion classification addresses these constraints. For effective learning and feature extraction, an upgraded encoder-decoder with sub-networks is interconnected, bringing the encoder feature maps relatively closer to the feature maps of the decoder. For pixel-wise categorization of melanoma lesions, the system uses a multi-scale and multi-stage technique, as well as a soft-max classifier. A novel approach called Lesion-classifier divides lesions of skin into non- melanoma and melanoma on the basis of the findings of pixel-wise classification. These studies are on the ISIC 2017 dataset, with dice coefficient and accuracy of 92 and 95 percent, respectively, while on the PH2 datasets, the dice coefficient and accuracies are as 93 and 95 percent.

articleTitle: Improve decision-making process in Air Command and Control Systems with meteorological data fusion
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The decision-making process can be complex in critical environments because it is associated with uncertain conditions. Air operations, in particular, require an effective decision-making process to guarantee safety and efficiency, where in addition, external factors such as weather conditions re-strict operations or generate adverse effects on human lives, infrastructure, economic resources, and equipment. Therefore, this work introduces a computerized decision aid methodology, implementing data fusion for aircraft location, and detecting me-teorological phenomena to identify possible interactions between these two entities. For this, detecting meteorological phenomena uses satellite images, allowing the identification of dangerous meteorological phenomena for aviation, such as convective clouds and lightning. On the other hand, the fusion of data sources allows aircraft detection, location, and tracking. The resulting information is integrated into the Colombian Air Force's operational command and control system to support decision-making, helping to improve safety standards, with algorithms and methodologies based on operational experience, and aimed at the automatic identification of risks for air operation.

articleTitle: Speech signal analysis of COVID-19 patients via machine learning approach
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The novel coronavirus is the most crucial pandemic that has been faced in recent times. The pandemic has caused severe economic and social devastation, and due to the lack of experience, many countries have a huge burden to protect their people from the coronavirus. This virus spreads from person to person so easily via the droplets. Hence, it is hard to identify the virus if they do not show the symptoms; thus, the asymptomatic person can become a super spreader and spread the virus faster than a symptomatic person. It is essential to seek a technological-based application that can be globally used. Therefore, this paper proposes a machine learning-based speech signal processing application to identify the asymptomatic and mild symptomatic COVID-19 virus-infected individuals. The proposed method uses gammatone cepstral features along with eight machine learning methods for the classification task. Finally, the best-trained machine learning model will apply in a real-time-based speech signal processing application. The final results show that the K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) and Ensemble Bagged Tree (EBT) can provide better classification results than the other machine learning models.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing Happiness and Well-being in South Asia
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The current study analyzes the factors affecting people's happiness and well-being in South Asian countries. For this purpose, the primary data was collected from 900 households from Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh using a structured questionnaire with a random sampling technique. The PLE-SEM technique was employed to analyze the data. The study results revealed that all the independent variables serve a crucial role in the happiness and well-being of the people in South Asia. Out of the eight independent variables, the relationship stands the positive and highest significant factor, and education stands the positive and least significant factor in establishing the happiness and well-being of people in South Asia. Likewise, education plays a significant moderating role between engagement and happiness & well-being, and it could be used as a strategic tool to increase happiness and well-being in South Asia. The research provides insights to government, policy-makers, administrators, and practitioners to implement the people's happiness and well-being.

articleTitle: Risk Analysis in Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) by Using FMEA and FTA Method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: International Labour Organization reports that around 2, 3 million workers have died annually. It shows the high rate of work accidents that encourages a company to put more concerns on workers' safety. PT XYZ implements occupational safety and health (OSH) at all lines of the production process, particularly in the packing division. Yet, there are still plenty of work accidents are identified, such as dehydration, muscle injury, feet run over by bar hanger, and other risks that potentially could cause injuries or even deaths. This study aims to analyze the risk of OSH in the packing division. The researchers use job safety analysis (JSA) as a method to collect data by recording the work activities and the potencies of work accidents risks. Failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA) is employed to identify failure mode to work accident risks as well as their effects, then the fault tree analysis (FTA) method is utilized as an analysis method for improvement based on the value of the highest risk priority number (RPN). From the result of JSA methods, it is filtered 27 work accident risks for RPN calculation. Later, it can be concluded that the risk of “feet run over by bar hanger” is determined with the highest RPN value of 48. Based on the result of the FTA analysis, the top event, which is feet run over by the bar hanger includes 9 basic events that will be considered as a basis of the improvement recommendation for the company.

articleTitle: Production and quality control of Hybrid Manufacturing Remanufacturing System with stochastic return
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: This paper proposes a simulation-based optimization model addressing production and quality control in Hybrid Manufacturing Remanufacturing Systems (HMRS). Specifically, the challenging issue, in the remanufacturing context, of quality control under the stochastic nature of product returns is addressed. Experiments are conducted to measure the effect of the return rate variability on the system performances. The main finding is that when this variability is low, the impact of return rate uncertainty on the system performances remains minor. Hence investing in the costly market-driven product acquisition approach may be useless for a company which is not confronted to high variability in product returns. However, results showed that, when this return rate variability increases the critical stock level and optimal quality control changed considerably. Consequently, for a company that experiences such variability, acquiring returned products through the classic waste stream system may result in considerable increase of the total production cost.

articleTitle: COVID-19: A Closer Look at the MENABanking Sector
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The present article investigates the consequences of COVID-19 on the financial condition of the banking industry and economy of Middle East and North Africa (MENA) countries. The findings of the study reveals that the banks in the MENA region are deeply affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The study's findings are anticipated to shed light on the government's action to avoid the negative impact of this crisis, and to find out the effect by the covid19 on the banking performance in MENA countries, with insights and benefits in mobilizing appropriate resources to improve the economy performance. The impact on banking is so huge that the recovery looks far-fetched. Our results are consistent with the MENA quarterly banking report Q3 (2020). The results of the study will help the banks and financial institutions in the MENA region to devise the appropriate strategy that can lead them on the road to recovery.

articleTitle: Paradigm Shift of Promotional Strategy from Celebrity to Social CEO
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: This study focuses on exploring the promotional approaches more specifically the company's CEOs as a social influencer. The study revealed that large companies are launching their CEOs as a social influencer which significantly reduce the company's marketing cost as well as create a better product image and business volume. This article focuses on endorsing social CEOs as celebrity endorsers because they are more genuinely worried about their brand image and customer preferences, providing a higher profit margin at reduced costs. This article contributions significantly to the field of endorsement of brands through CEOs. Moreover, the study is also helpful for corporate and academics and serves as an incentive for further studies in this area. Meanwhile, there are also possibilities for researchers to re-conceptualize some of the widely accepted areas of social CEOs in promotional strategy.

articleTitle: Literature Survey on Adaptive Virtual Machine Scheduling Strategy to Optimize Load Balancing in Cloud Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Cloud computing has become a widely accepted technology that provides on-demand services. Resource man-agement is critical in cloud computing to provide required resources to the subscribers. Cloud computing uses virtualization technology to optimize resource utilization. Resource allocation is done based on virtual machines. Load balancing based on virtual machine strategy is a more challenging problem. Heavy Workload of the physical machine decreases the VM s performance and increases the job completion time. It enables virtual machine migration techniques with the help of load balancing methods to remove hotspots and associations for the improvement of resource utilization and energy efficiency. In this paper, the survey is done on various load balancing mechanisms and their shortcomings are presented.

articleTitle: Development of a novel Decision-Making tool for vessel efficiency optimization using IoT and DL
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The era of the Internet of Things and big data has completely changed the landscape of many scientific disciplines. Embracing the big data revolution, machine learning techniques seem to have substituted traditional physics-based models due to their effectiveness and flexibility. According to Rolls-Royce [1], the smart ship will revolutionize the landscape of ship design and operations, the same way smartphones did our daily life. These enhanced data-driven analytics yield substantial benefits in terms of cost savings by limiting the degree to which human factor intervenes to perform certain operations, and also by providing reliable and accurate information in real-time information regarding the operational health of the machinery on board, ensuring the safety of the crew as well as the reliability of the equipment. [2]. Despite its importance, the majority of efforts towards this direction are limited to academic efforts or black-box approaches. In the current work, a distributed software platform that augments the decision-making process within the shipping industry is critically presented. Key technological pillars are Big Data technologies, data fusion, and large-scale deep learning-based processing techniques. Evaluation of the platform, based on actual case data, provides evidence of its capacity for diagnosis and anomaly detection on the operation of critical subsystems.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric Generators as Alternate Energy Source in Heating Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: There is a lot of energy wasted in the industries in the form of heat but in that only 35% is converted into electrical energy but rest of the heat is not utilized. The main aim of the paper is to produce electrical power from refineries where energy wastage is more common in this paper the complete work is basically following the principle of the Seebeck effect in which the voltage is generated between two dissimilar semiconductors at different temperatures. The high voltage difference is produced by the thermoelectric module at very high temperatures. In this, the generated energy is by heating the source using a candle. The designed module is to produce a small voltage for consumer electronic devices in absence of sun and wind energy. In this paper the maximum output voltage produced by the thermoelectric module is approximately DC 9.8 V (Series) and 2.6 V (Parallel), The total power generated is approximately 7.5 W (Series) and 7.6 W (Parallel), and the maximum current produced approximately is 0.77 A (Series) and 2.88 A (Parallel) in the model, these results are confirmed with theoretical values at fixed resistance.

articleTitle: Predicting Daily Closing Value of Indian Stock Index Through Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Investments in equity market are risky but highly rewarding with attractive returns provided the investors are able to predict the future direction of the stock price movements. The present study aims to predict whether the daily closing values of stock index will be in bullish mode or bearish mode. The Artificial Neural Networks is applied in this study with eight Technical Indicators to predict daily closing values of NIFTY 50 Index. The results show the predictions of closing trend of NIFTY 50 with 80% accuracy which is very good for a large sample size of 1408 trading days. The model predicted the bullish trend with 82.8% and bearish trend with 76.3% accuracy level for the large data points applied in the model. The percentage of incorrect predictions over the training and testing data set is within the acceptable limit. The normalized importance level of eight technical indicators ranges from 21.2 % to 110% shows the relevance of the technical indicators applied as independent variables.

articleTitle: Mathematical Analysis of Optimal Cost-Effective Control of COVID-19: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Currently, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic is a worldwide health issue. In this paper, a nonlinear optimal control problem for COVID-19 is formulated by extending an existing mathematical deterministic model involving 8-dimensional autonomous system of differential equations analysed for the disease spread in Malaysia. The new model includes three time-dependent variables measuring the levels of preventive, treatment and management controls. Pontryagin's maximum principle is used to determine the necessary conditions required for the existence of optimal control triplet. The effect of different control strategies on the dynamics of the disease spread is measured through the numerical implementation of the derived optimality system. Cost-effectiveness analysis is conducted to ascertain the most cost-effective strategy required to curtail the spread of COVID-19 in the population.

articleTitle: Development of Corporate Mobility by Small Business Entities and Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The use of information and communication technology is becoming more and more widespread and penetrates almost all business processes of any company, it is important to note new trends that have manifested themselves especially vividly during the period when the remote format of work of most enterprises and organizations has become an urgent need. It is the new trends in the use of information and communication technologies by small enterprises that have become the subject of consideration in this article. The purpose of this study was to identify the opportunities that open up for small enterprises when implementing and using corporate mobility, taking into account the specifics of the business model of small business entity. Ensuring business mobility, including it in the overall business strategy is a complex and multifaceted problem that is at the stage of practical solution and theoretical justification.

articleTitle: Drones Technology for Sustainable Decisions & Development to Redress Illegal Logging
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Illegal logging has continuously haunted many countries including Brunei Darussalam resulting in significant financial losses over the years to the Brunei government. With Brunei having to possess high -grade Gaharu agarwood trees in its untouched virgin forest, illegal loggers and forest intruders posed a security threat to security authorities. This paper assesses the opportunities in deploying drones to assist in sustainable development by preventing illegal logging activities within Brunei forest. Doing so, a qualitative approach was used to interview and collect data from various public agencies involved in combating and ways to improve in preventing illegal logging activities. Deploying drones technology will support sustainable decisions to enhance the current mode of operation in redressing illegal logging. The drone has gone a long way since it was introduced and its rapid technological development has brought success to many operations worldwide. The result of this paper has shown evidence that drones would be a cost-effective alternative to redress capability gap to tackle illegal logging in Brunei.

articleTitle: Fuzzy sports motivational system for measuring psychological and training issues in running recreational practice and adherence
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: A fuzzy system for assessing sports adherence and practice by taking into account motivational training and psy-chological factors for recreational runners is proposed in this paper. Running is a sport that has continuously been increasing and recreational runners, mostly characterized by amateur ath-letes, are characterized as presenting diverse and multifaceted profile. Such running sports practitioners present interests from promotion of health and attending races up to achieve social interaction and obtain pleasant moments. In consonance with this perspective, the proposed fuzzy IF-THEN system is designed by employing psychological and practice aspects to assess the level of interest, motivation, and adherence of recreational runners. In this sense, the fuzzy inference system uses as linguistic input variables the psychological level of satisfaction concerning the training in group (collective training) and coach's professional expertise (professional quality of the coach), two prominent motivation factors among recreational sports practitioners. The fuzzy set theory and fuzzy logic is used to represent the subtle and subjective reasoning concerning the sport perception. Such a fuzzy motivational assessment enables to stratify and score, by qualitatively and quantitatively measure, the impact in the adherence in the sports practice of recreational runners.

articleTitle: The Impact of Family, Lifestyle, and COVID-19 Factors on Private High School Students' Academic Performance: Data Mining Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Bahrain private high schools currently face a significant gap in identifying trends that impact students' learning outcome. Currently, Bahrain's Education and Training Quality Authority (BQA) is tasked with evaluating educational institutions' infrastructure and technology availability's impact on learning outcomes, overlooking factors such as family lifestyle, students' time allocation, health, and COVID-19 related factors. This study aims to identify trends that influence Bahraini private high school students' learning outcomes and measure the extent these factors impact to raise actionable recommendations. Specifically, this research implements Decision Tree (DT), Density-Based Clustering (DBC) and Linear Regression (LR) to identify such trends. In this context, learning outcomes are identified as average grades, which serve as an indicator of the knowledge retained. This study's results found that family life; parents' educational level in particular, has the most influential impact on student grades, while for time allocation, students must pay attention to their time management skills to ensure a balance trade-off between recreational activities and studying; not over allocate time to a specific activity. Finally, and interestingly, COVID-19 had minimal impact on student performance.

articleTitle: A Distributed Non-elitist Evolutionary Scalable Asynchronous Rebuilding Algorithm for Solving Pickup and Delivery Problems with Time Windows
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The pickup and delivery problem with time windows (PDPTW) is an NP-hard problem. It is a conundrum challenge to solve this problem that consistently produces near-optimal results with the least difference in magnitude. This paper presents a distributed non-elitist evolutionary scalable asynchronous rebuilding algorithm (DNESARA) to solve PDPTW. This algorithm allows the non-elitist evolutionary algorithm to perform scalable asynchronous rebuilding algorithms for a speedy attainment of high-performance solutions and take advantage of divergence and convergence power of the non-elitist evolutionary and asynchronous rebuilding algorithm. Our experiments use comprehensive Li and Lim instances and benchmarks against published algorithms and best-known solutions. The high-quality results produced by DNESARA outperform the best-known solutions, three published algorithms.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of an Intelligent Fuzzy Logic Controller for a Nonlinear Dynamic System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Owing to storage, mixing and blending tasks carried out in process industries with spherical tank systems (STIS), the need arises for liquid level control to ensure quality of production, less reaction losses and safety. For this reason, this paper proposes the design of intelligent fuzzy logic controllers to solve the liquid level control problem. Using MATLAB Fuzzy Inference System and Simulink, four fuzzy logic control (FLC) design schemes have been developed with liquid level, error, liquid level change rate and error change rate as inputs. The optimized controller proposed is a hybridization of FLC and Proportional-Integral (PI) control abbreviated (PI-Like FLC). The results showed the PI-Like FLC had superior performance with respect to settling time and steady state error compared to other schemes. The steady state error was found to be 0.0082 and further optimization resulted in an error drop of 95 percent with disturbance rejection of 3000s at inflow range of 61 to 90 cube meters per second.

articleTitle: Measuring the impact of COVID-19 on Automotive Supply Chain using the SCOR model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019(COVID-19) has the potential to destroy individual livelihoods, businesses, industries, and entire economies. The automotive sector is not immune to these impacts, and the crisis is starting to have serious consequences in the short, medium, and long term for the industry. In this sense, this exploratory study examines the overall impacts of the coronavirus pandemic on the Supply Chain (SC) of automotive industries. A listing of the adverse effects of COVID-19 on the automotive SC has been highlighted. This study also measures using the SCOR model the impact of the coronavirus pandemic on the four poles of the SC such as import, production, sale, and export. The study also aimed to propose a roadmap-oriented Industry 4.0 to reduce the impact of COVID-19

Author Keywords: The COVID-19 pandemic has had far-reaching health and financial consequences. This study aimed to measure the impact of COVID-19 on the SC of the automotive sector by following the SCOR model architecture and to propose recommendations in the strategy and vision of the SC to resist such a crisis in the future

articleTitle: COVID-19 Pandemic Effect on Financial Stability: Evidence from GCC Countries
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The study aims to investigate the impact of a number of macroeconomic and bank-specific factors along with the most recent global factor, i.e., COVID-19 pandemic on the financial stability in GCC economies. The sample consists of 32 domestic conventional banks for the period spanning 2011 to 2020, generating a panel sample of 320 observations. An application of System GMM estimate provides a strong evidence of the effect of the pandemic on nonperforming loans (NPLs) in the short-run despite limited observations with only 1-year data. However, pandemic has relatively less significant impact in the long-run. As expected, both credit growth rate and inflation rate have significant negative impact on NPLs.

articleTitle: A Decision Support Systemfor Commercial Lending
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: Decision processes are activities mostly periodic, repetitiveand time consuming. This brings experts to refer to their knowledge of past experiences. Developing a knowledge base clearly facilitates the similar subsequent recommendations actions and reduces greatly the time necessary to make a decision, especially in constrained tine applications. In this paper, we propose a knowledge-based decision support system called BL-KBDSS where rules and procedures used by the experts in past experience are stored in a knowledge base and managed by a case-based reasoner. We are experimenting with our approach in financial field, more precisely, to commercial lending, a semi-structured. BL-KBDSS will support experts to make decisions and compensate for the lack of experience of young bank officers. II will also disseminate the experience available on various bankingagencies.

articleTitle: Detected pulses from the motion of the head to estimate heartbeat rate
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Decision Aid Sciences and Application (DASA)
abstract: The beating of the heart sends blood throughout the body to feed the cells and puts pressure on the blood vessel walls. Therefore, monitoring this process is extremely important in the diagnosis and treatment of the disease. In the past, people did this by counting pulses of artery or wearing of heart monitor on the body. In both of these cases, physical contact with the body is required to get the heart rate. Today, with the advancement of science and technology, we can overcome these limitations based on computer vision techniques. This paper proposes one such method - measuring heartbeat rate through frequent pulses from the motion of blood vessel on the head. We extract them from a regular computer's camera in real-time. Our method identifies and records the oscillation of the feature points. Then, using the algorithm principal component analysis decays their trajectories into a group of component motions. Thus, we can determine the best component corresponding to heartbeats based on its frequency. In order to do that, we built an electrocardiogram and analyzed it to identify the peaks of the trajectory, which corresponded to the heartbeats. Based on that data, we calculated the subject's heartbeat rate. When evaluated on 10 subjects, our approach reports heartbeat rate roughly the same as a conventional sphygmomanometer. This result shows that the proposed method is correct, robust, and economically suitable. However, in order to achieve high technical efficiency without changing the economy, this method needs to be further improved in the future.
